synopsis: Across the corpus, simulation complements rather than eliminates physical testing: it selects tests deserving scarce prototype time and expands evidence around physical anchors, while documented validation programmes retain physical tests and staged field operation [f11311, f484, f309]. Exhaustive field coverage of more than 7,000 validation cells is infeasible, so simulation or HIL should supply large stratified trial counts, with physical validation in each stratum and smaller-sample independent confirmation [f5207, f6889]. Substitution is defensible only inside a measured, independently reviewed credibility envelope; physical confirmation remains necessary at boundaries, after influential changes, and where models are weak [f10467, f7536, f10470]. On-road precedents retain physical checks: Euro NCAP's 2026 Virtual Testing protocol, version 1.00 dated March 2025, requires randomly selected physical verification after simulation predictions, but no prescribed simulation share or off-road regulatory acceptance of simulation-based rate claims was found [f1216, f4316, f6931]. For a four-month off-road validation programme, the recommended approach is an analytical safety case with targeted physical tests and credible simulation, organized as an integrated strategy; the principal calendar saving comes from moving work before prototype availability, not removing physical validation [f2137, f9555, f311].
